$comment: Which display panels an ESP32 board can drive: the data behind the
`device` setting a control plane pushes to an ESP32 (docs/cloud-frames.md,
the `set_settings` row). Edit THIS file, then run
`python3 frameos/tools/generate_esp32_board_panels.py`: it adds the panels
the firmware compiles in (embedded/esp32/components/frameos_display/
generate_panel_table.py, panel_catalog) and writes the firmware's board
table (C), the cloud's and the SPA's (TS). The backend suite runs it with
`--check`, and checks every ESP32 hardware preset table against this one.
`boards` names every ESP32 hardware preset (`set hardware <name>` on the
USB console). `panel` is the firmware's panel name the preset applies.
`display`:
builtin    the panel is part of the board; a push may name that panel
and no other, since any other would drive a display that is
not there.
connector  a driver board with a panel socket; a push may name any
compiled panel the board's wiring can drive.
The rule, the same in fos_board_panels.c, lib/esp32-board-panels.ts and
utils/esp32BoardPanels.ts (conformance cases: the `panels` section of
docs/cloud-frames-fixtures.json). A pushed panel is refused with the first
reason that applies:
panel_off        "none": turning the panel off is done on the frame
(USB console or setup portal), where someone can turn
it back on.
not_compiled     this firmware has no driver for the panel.
builtin_display  the board's preset has its display built in, and the
push names another panel.
no_wiring        the board's display pins are not set (neither the SPI
set rst/dc/cs/busy/sck/mosi nor the I2C pair sck/mosi
with cs/dc/busy unset).
wrong_bus        the panel is driven on the other bus.
needs_cs2        the panel needs a second chip-select and pins.cs2 is
not wired.
A board whose preset is not listed here (a custom build, or a preset from
a newer control plane) is judged by its wiring alone.
